Surgery Information.Surgery Procedure: bilateral mastectomies with left axillary lymph node dissection
Surgery Information.Surgery Findings: IDC multifocal, SBR grade 2 and 1, largest focus 3.9 cm, margins negative; Ductal carcinoma in situ, intermediate nuclear grade, metastatic carcinoma to two lymph nodes (2/2), 1.5 cm largest deposit, microcalcifications in association with ductal carcinoma in situ and benign ducts

Symptoms or Side Effects.Side Effect: slight more arm stiffness on her left arm
numbness near her left axilla and left elbow post-operatively

Additional Comments: The patient is a 70-year-old female with a history of hypertension (HTN) and hyperlipidemia (HLD). She has a strong family history of breast cancer on her paternal side, with her paternal grandmother having passed away from breast cancer in her 60s and her sister having undergone a double mastectomy for breast cancer. Her father has Jewish heritage, which raises the possibility of a BRCA mutation. The patient has not previously undergone genetic testing but has agreed to pursue genetic counseling and testing. She has been feeling well since her surgery, with slight arm stiffness and some numbness near her left axilla and elbow, which are improving.
